old: A remembered direction must remain useful after its cue disappears; the eyes must hold an angle while an animal looks at a target; a moving animal must keep track of where it is. These tasks depend on groups of [**neuron**]{.definition-term custom-style="Definition Term"}s, the brain's signaling cells, whose electrical signals are brief and variable. Computational and systems neuroscience studies how these cells and their interactions support such behavior. Mathematical models connect assumptions about cells and their interactions to predictions; recordings test those predictions against neural activity and movement. The three papers use these methods to study different parts of the problem: maintaining a value, locating the source of an irregular movement, and explaining the spatial patterns through which cells represent position.
